info.title: fal.minimax-music-3.v1
info.description: fal endpoint minimax/music-3, model fal:minimax/music-3, through the Livepeer fal route adapter. The request and output schemas are fal's own, from its public queue OpenAPI (x-source), with long descriptions shortened and examples and fal's UI hints left out. Behavior is fal.queue.v1's.

post.description: The body is fal's input for minimax/music-3, forwarded to fal unchanged; a success answer carries fal's output under `output`. Behaves as fal.queue.v1 describes. Each URL output pointer names the URL itself, and a `*` stands for every item of a list. URL fields nested deeper aren't listed in inputs or outputs; the schemas show them.

fal.summary: Built from fal's own example and default values

value.prompt: Genre: acoustic pop. BPM: 96. Key: C major. Warm and intimate, building gently into the chorus. Vocals: soft female lead, close and breathy, light stacked harmonies in the chorus. Arrangement: fingerpicked guitar and soft piano; brushed drums and upright bass enter in the chorus.
value.lyrics:
[verse]
Morning light filtering through the pine
Every quiet street is yours and mine
[chorus]
Softly the world begins to breathe

200.description: fal's result, or an error that came after the headers were sent. The body tells them apart: a result has `output`, an error has `error`.

4XX.description: Refused before fal accepted the request: the body is too large, or fal refused it at submit

5XX.description: fal failed or was unreachable at submit, or the deadline passed before fal accepted the request

errors.note: The adapter's deadline passed: before fal accepted the request (a 504 with no request ID), or while fal was working (a 200 with error.status 504). fal may still finish and charge the operator; once fal has accepted it, the request ID is in the header and at /request_id
fal refused the input, at submit or when its result was read after queueing (then in a 200); fal's detail is in /error/upstream_body
fal refused the request, at submit or when its result was read after queueing
The body is larger than the adapter's max_request_bytes, which the operator sets (1 MiB by default)

In a 200: fal reported that the request failed or reached an unknown state, or its status couldn't be read; error.status is fal's status, or 502. Unknown: how fal's status marks an input it refuses after queueing, so such refusals land here too; fal's detail is in /error/upstream_body
In a 200: fal finished, but its result couldn't be read; error.status is fal's status, or 502. The result may still be collectable with the request ID
At submit: fal refused the operator's fal key
At submit: fal refused the operator's fal key for this endpoint
At submit: fal doesn't know the pinned endpoint
At submit: fal is limiting the operator's requests
At submit: fal was unreachable, or answered without a request ID; fal may have queued the request, and no request ID came back
At submit: fal timed out; it may have queued the request, and no request ID came back

cost_hint.note: A call costs the runner's fixed PriceInfo, charged when the node reserves the call, before the adapter runs and whatever the outcome. The answer's billable_units is fal's own count for the request, from its X-Fal-Billable-Units header (null when absent), in a unit that differs by endpoint: a receipt to compare afterwards, not the wholesale charge.

recovery.note: The header comes with the answer's headers as soon as fal accepts the request, and the body repeats it at /request_id. The adapter has no operation that returns a late result and keeps nothing once it has answered. Collecting one needs fal's queue API (GET https://queue.fal.run/<fal app>/requests/<request ID>, where the fal app is the endpoint ID's first two segments, or three under comfy/ and workflows/) and the operator's fal key, so today only the operator can collect a late result. With sync_mode set, fal keeps no copy to collect.

x-livepeer.readiness: The adapter has loaded its pinned endpoint's route and schema bundle and holds the operator's fal key. It doesn't call fal, so it doesn't yet check the vendor as SPEC asks of a proxy; unknown whether it will.
